items.analysis: Walter Reed continues to receive U.S. military casualties from Operation EPIC FURY—13 additional wounded personnel arrived via Ramstein Air Base and Joint Base Andrews for extended care. The transfers occur as regional tensions escalate sharply, with President Trump ordering CENTCOM to 'open the gates of hell' on Iran and the State Department issuing a worldwide caution. U.S. officials are worried that the increasing accuracy of Iranian strikes on American bases may stem from military or intelligence cooperation with Russia or China, the Wall Street Journal reported. Separately, the Trump administration has been scaling back some sanctions on Russia, wary that overusing such measures could encourage de-dollarization, the New York Times reported, even as those Iran accuracy concerns involve possible Moscow cooperation. The broader security landscape includes a tentatively agreed nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia that awaits President Trump's signature; the deal would allow uranium enrichment without the strongest IAEA inspection protocol, and plans to redirect U.S. foreign aid toward politically aligned projects, including a $40 million grant for the Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation, are also under review. Domestically, the Justice Department has lifted its ban on TikTok for government devices, a court review found that half of ICE's assault charges against protesters have collapsed, and new data show the number of Americans not in the labor force reaching an all-time high of 105.8 million.

items.title: Imam Khomeini Hussainiya, Tehran, Iran: U.S. officials expressed concern that Iran may be receiving targeting data and assistance from China or Russia, according to The Wall Street Journal.
items.description: U.S. officials expressed concern that Iran may be receiving targeting data and assistance from China or Russia, according to The Wall Street Journal.
items.rawSummary: Statements from Tehran's Imam Khomeini Hussainiya marked a sharp escalation as Iran suspended its interim memorandum of understanding with the U.S., threatened full-scale war, and U.S. forces concluded an eighth consecutive night of strikes.
items.analysis: Statements from the Hussainiya marked a sharp escalation when senior advisor Mohsen Rezaee initially declared the dual-track policy of war and negotiation a dead end, warning that U.S. landings would trigger efforts to destroy American forces beyond Iran's borders; he later told state broadcaster IRIB that if U.S. strikes continue for two or three more days, Iran will shift to a full-scale offensive, abandoning its reciprocal-only posture and pledging waves of missiles and drones. The IRGC claimed retaliatory strikes on U.S. bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, and elsewhere—Kuwait confirmed infrastructure damage—and threatened to expand targeting to industrial, IT, and AI assets of companies with U.S. shareholders, while Iranian authorities separately warned they would strike American businesses in the region if U.S. strikes hit civilian infrastructure. Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi suspended the Pakistan-brokered memorandum of understanding and Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei accused the United States of repeated violations and promised 'unforgettable lessons.' Footage showed U.S. forces launching ATACMS missiles from a location reportedly in Kuwait toward Iran, and American officials told CBS News that a new round of strikes would be more extensive than previous ones, following the U.S. military's confirmation of two service members killed in Jordan while defending against Iranian ballistic missiles and drones. U.S. officials further told The Wall Street Journal that Iran has begun adapting its ballistic missiles to travel at extremely high speeds and maneuver during reentry, challenging American air defense systems, and raised concerns that Iran may be receiving targeting data and assistance from China or Russia. Domestic pressures from the rial’s collapse and protest-related executions compound the regime’s challenges, and the Supreme National Security Council has ordered media to suppress details of civilian damage. President Trump, in remarks following the deaths, called the losses 'very sad' but reiterated that Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon; he later dismissed Iran's suspension of the interim agreement as something he 'couldn't care less.' Overnight, U.S. forces completed an eighth consecutive night of strikes, moving closer to the threshold Iran’s leadership described as a trigger for abandoning restraint.

items.rawSummary: U.S. strikes on Iranian transport infrastructure and a naval blockade are being met by Iranian missile attacks across the Gulf, with new strikes reported on Qeshm Island and ongoing commercial-ship harassment in the Strait of Hormuz as diplomatic calls for an unconditional reopening of the strait intensify.
items.analysis: The U.S. campaign targeting bridges, railroads and other infrastructure aims to cut supply routes to the IRGC Navy's Bandar Abbas hub, with overnight strikes also hitting Qeshm Island, according to Iran's Tasnim news agency. The naval blockade has sharply reduced Strait of Hormuz traffic, while Iran struck Kuwaiti infrastructure, U.S. assets across the Gulf—including a base in Saudi Arabia for the first time in months—and a former base in Syria. An Iranian missile attack on a Jordanian airbase killed two U.S. service members. Iran's IRGC also fired on commercial vessels, with conflicting accounts over mine explosions that CENTCOM denied, while Iranian media said the IRGC fired missiles at a vessel from Bandar Abbas. U.S. officials suspect China or Russia may be providing targeting data, as Iran has begun using high-speed, maneuverable missiles to penetrate defenses. Meanwhile, Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei declared the U.S.-Iran memorandum of understanding null, citing irreconcilable differences over the Strait of Hormuz clause, and the EU and Gulf states have called for the strait to remain permanently open without conditions.

items.title: Iran (Ahvaz, Chabahar), Iran: U.S. officials assessed that Iran has adapted to American air defenses by using faster, more maneuverable missiles that are harder to intercept, and expressed concern that targeting support from China or Russia may be enabling the improved accuracy, though no evidence has been made public, the Wall Street Journal reported.
items.description: U.S. officials assessed that Iran has adapted to American air defenses by using faster, more maneuverable missiles that are harder to intercept, and expressed concern that targeting support from China or Russia may be enabling the improved accuracy, though no evidence has been made public, the Wall Street Journal reported.
items.rawSummary: A massive new wave of U.S. airstrikes struck multiple locations across Iran, including Hormozgan and Khuzestan provinces, while Iranian retaliatory strikes hit Gulf state targets and killed U.S. troops in Jordan, drawing threats of regional escalation.
items.analysis: U.S. airstrikes on Iran escalated into an eighth night as CENTCOM launched a new and far more expansive wave of strikes, reportedly ordered by President Trump to 'rain hell' on Iran in retaliation for the killing of two American servicemen in a ballistic missile attack on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan. Strikes were reported across wide areas, including Ahvaz, Lar, Yazd, Bandar Abbas, and Qeshm overnight, and later Sirik, Garuk, Bandar-e Lengeh, and Behbahan, with internet outages reported in parts of Hormozgan Province. The IRGC earlier struck targets in Kuwait and Bahrain, hitting a police academy and causing airport closure, and warned that any Gulf state hosting U.S. forces used against Iran would face a corresponding response, naming specific bases across the region. U.S. officials assessed that Iran is employing faster, more maneuverable missiles that are harder to intercept, and the Wall Street Journal reported concerns that China or Russia may be providing targeting support, though no evidence has been made public. The conflict unfolds against a backdrop of severe economic distress in Iran, where the rial has collapsed and a confidential government report indicates only a small fraction of the population supports the status quo.

items.title: Beijing, China, China: China acquired an estimated 48 tonnes of gold via the London OTC market in May, the largest monthly purchase in over a year, according to Goldman Sachs; the central bank also officially added 15 tonnes in June, extending its streak of reserve increases to 20 consecutive months, though actual accumulation is likely far higher.

items.rawSummary: China's economic slowdown deepened amid slumping property investment and weak consumption, while it navigated geopolitical pressures by calling for Iran conflict de-escalation, suspending Russia pipeline talks, and denying US election interference, even as a favorable global survey and an AI model launch offered bright spots and it quietly expanded gold reserves.
items.analysis: China’s economy is experiencing broad strain, with second-quarter GDP growth slowing to 4.3% and fixed-asset investment contracting 5.7% in the first half, driven by a record 18% plunge in property investment, while retail sales and auto purchases remain weak. Domestic demand fragility is compounded by a 41% year-on-year drop in crude oil imports to a ten-year low, partly due to the Iran conflict’s supply disruption. Geopolitically, Beijing called for safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz and a US-Iran ceasefire in coordination with Pakistan, denied US election interference claims ahead of a planned Xi visit, and suspended Power of Siberia 2 pipeline talks, undermining Russian energy ambitions. A Pew survey shows China now viewed more favorably than the United States across six continents, but the economic outlook remains clouded. In the tech sector, Moonshot AI launched the world’s largest open-weight AI model, and quietly, China has been accumulating gold at a pace far exceeding official central bank figures, signalling a strategic push to diversify reserves.

Domestically, the Justice Department has lifted its ban on TikTok for government devices, a court review found that half of ICE's assault charges against protesters have collapsed, and new data show the number of Americans not in the labor force reaching an all-time high of 105.8 million.

items.title: Imam Khomeini Hussainiya, Tehran, Iran: U.S. forces concluded an eighth consecutive night of strikes against Iran.
items.description: U.S. forces concluded an eighth consecutive night of strikes against Iran.
items.rawSummary: Statements from Tehran's Imam Khomeini Hussainiya marked a sharp escalation as Iran suspended its interim memorandum of understanding with the U.S., threatened full-scale war, and U.S. forces concluded an eighth consecutive night of strikes.
items.analysis: Statements from the Hussainiya marked a sharp escalation when senior advisor Mohsen Rezaee initially declared the dual-track policy of war and negotiation a dead end, warning that U.S. landings would trigger efforts to destroy American forces beyond Iran's borders; he later told state broadcaster IRIB that if U.S. strikes continue for two or three more days, Iran will shift to a full-scale offensive, abandoning its reciprocal-only posture and pledging waves of missiles and drones. The IRGC claimed retaliatory strikes on U.S. bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, and elsewhere—Kuwait confirmed infrastructure damage—and threatened to expand targeting to industrial, IT, and AI assets of companies with U.S. shareholders, while Iranian authorities separately warned they would strike American businesses in the region if U.S. strikes hit civilian infrastructure. Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi suspended the Pakistan-brokered memorandum of understanding and Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei accused the United States of repeated violations and promised 'unforgettable lessons.' Footage showed U.S. forces launching ATACMS missiles from a location reportedly in Kuwait toward Iran, and American officials told CBS News that a new round of strikes would be more extensive than previous ones, following the U.S. military's confirmation of two service members killed in Jordan while defending against Iranian ballistic missiles and drones. U.S. officials further told The Wall Street Journal that Iran has begun adapting its ballistic missiles to travel at extremely high speeds and maneuver during reentry, challenging American air defense systems, and raised concerns that Iran may be receiving targeting data and assistance from China or Russia. Domestic pressures from the rial’s collapse and protest-related executions compound the regime’s challenges, and the Supreme National Security Council has ordered media to suppress details of civilian damage. President Trump, in remarks following the deaths, called the losses 'very sad' but reiterated that Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon; he later dismissed Iran's suspension of the interim agreement as something he 'couldn't care less.' Overnight, U.S. forces completed an eighth consecutive night of strikes, moving closer to the threshold Iran’s leadership described as a trigger for abandoning restraint.
